\noindent{\LARGE\bfseries Figure 1. DTAG architecture and one-step greedy question selection}
\vspace{.35cm}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[>=Latex,thick,font=\small,
  box/.style={draw=black,rounded corners=2pt,align=center,minimum height=1.1cm,inner sep=7pt},
  arrow/.style={->,draw=black,line width=1.1pt}]
  \filldraw[fill=dtpale!35,draw=dtblue,dashed,rounded corners=6pt] (0,0) rectangle (10.2,-9.9);
  \filldraw[fill=dtmint!48,draw=teal!65!black,dashed,rounded corners=6pt] (10.45,0) rectangle (36.5,-9.9);
  \node[anchor=north west,font=\Large\bfseries,text=dtblue] at (.3,-.25){LLM layer: semantic interface};
  \node[anchor=north west,font=\Large\bfseries,text=teal!50!black] at (10.85,-.25){Digital twin (DT): conditional model and state};
  \node[box,fill=dtpale] (q) at (2.35,-2.35) {Natural-language\\question $q_t$};
  \node[box,fill=dtpale,text width=4.6cm] (parse) at (7.15,-2.35)
    {\textbf{LLM grounding}\\semantic mapping to survey item $v$};
  \draw[arrow] (q)--(parse);
  \node[box,fill=dtpale,text width=6.2cm] (prose) at (5.1,-7.6)
    {\textbf{LLM verbalization}\\grounded categorical answer and next-question wording};
  \node[box,fill=dtmint,text width=4.9cm] (state) at (14.2,-2.2)
    {\textbf{DT state $s_t$}\\observed categorical anchors};
  \node[box,fill=dtmint,text width=5.6cm] (condition) at (21,-2.2)
    {\textbf{Native LSM}\\$p_\Phi(a\mid s_t,v)$};
  \node[box,fill=dtmint,text width=6.2cm] (geometry) at (29.5,-2.2)
    {\textbf{Predictive phenotype and geometry}\\$I_\Phi(s_t)$; unasked-response probabilities};
  \draw[arrow] (parse)--(state);
  \draw[arrow] (state)--(condition);
  \draw[arrow] (condition)--(geometry);
  \node[box,fill=dtorange,draw=dtred,line width=1.3pt,text width=17.2cm,minimum height=2.8cm] (opt) at (23.5,-5.35)
    {\Large\textbf{One-step greedy question selection}\\[3pt]
     For each eligible unanswered item $v$, enumerate categorical answers $a$;\\
     compute $\displaystyle\mu_v(s_t)=\sum_a p_\Phi(a\mid s_t,v)
       \left[I_\Phi(s_t\cup\{v=a\})-I_\Phi(s_t)\right]$;\\
     choose $\displaystyle v^\star=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_v\mu_v(s_t)$ (right),
     $\operatorname*{arg\,min}_v\mu_v(s_t)$ (left),\\
     or $\displaystyle \operatorname*{arg\,min}_v|\mu_v(s_t)|$ (neutral).
    };
  \draw[arrow] (condition.south) |- (opt.north west);
  \draw[arrow] (geometry.south) |- (opt.north east);
  \node[box,fill=dtmint,text width=6.1cm] (selected) at (19,-8.4)
     {\textbf{Selected item $v^\star$}\\sample observed $a_t\sim p_\Phi(\cdot\mid s_t,v^\star)$};
  \node[box,fill=dtmint,text width=6.8cm] (update) at (30,-8.4)
     {\textbf{Anchor and update}\\$s_{t+1}=s_t\cup\{v^\star=a_t\}$};
  \draw[arrow] (opt.south) -- (selected.north);
  \draw[arrow] (selected)--(update);
  \draw[arrow] (selected.west) -- (prose.east);
  \draw[arrow] (update.east) -- ++(2,0) |- (state.east);
  \draw[arrow,dashed] (prose.west) -| (q.south);
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\noindent\textbf{Figure 1.} DTAG separates the LLM language interface from the native conditional digital twin.
The greedy optimizer scores \emph{the next question only} under the current state; no long-horizon optimization or human attitude intervention is implied.
\par\vfill
\clearpage

\noindent\textbf{Figure 2.} Mean net changes in the pole-relative native LSM index for four adaptive policies.
Error whiskers and shaded regions are 95\% bootstrap confidence intervals across 40 synthetic repetitions per persona and policy.
The LSM conditionals, rather than real human belief transitions, determine the responses.

\noindent\textbf{Figure 3.} \emph{Left}: all 18 question-identity heatmaps (six personas by three adaptive policies),
displaying 40 runs over 20 positions; a single globally optimized index maps 161 displayed questions from a
228-question catalog (identities are categorical, not metric distances). \emph{Right}: paired signed endpoint
differences and 95\% paired bootstrap intervals for reverse and two shuffled fixed-question permutations
(20 items per set, 40 repetitions per order). Zero mean does not imply pathwise order invariance.
